Regions and Societies — Realistic Planets 2 edition Official Wiki and Documentation: https://github.com/Regions-and-societies/Core-MMF/wiki
This is the Realistic Planets 2 build of Regions and Societies. It is identical to the standard mod except that it runs on the map-mode framework bundled with Realistic Planets 2 instead of the standalone Map Mode Framework. Use this edition if you play with Realistic Planets 2; use the standard edition otherwise. Do not run both editions, or both frameworks, at once.
Regions and Societies overhauls the world map into living geography: dynamic geographic provinces with terrain-aware borders that follow the land, four-tier faction territory ownership, geography-driven faction placement you set up before you generate the world, and full regional demographics across seven axes with their own map overlays - built on Realistic Planets 2's bundled map-mode framework. It is the continuation of Regions and Territories under a new identity.
Features: - Geographic Domain Mapping: splits the world into dynamic provinces whose borders follow the terrain - coasts, mountain ridges and biome edges - with inland lakes shared between their shores and small islands folded into the mainland; every region is one connected landmass. - Territorial Ownership: a four-tier ladder from exclusive hold to loose claim, shaded on the map; a faction that holds half a region earns its natural barriers - coasts, rock and ridges - as a secure border. - Geography-Driven Faction Placement: nations settle by a biome's real liveability, cluster or scatter to taste, and scattered low-tech peoples split into regional kin factions. Set every faction's share of the world in the new-game Geographic Placement dialog. - Regional Demographics: every region carries a deterministic demographic profile - age structure, sex ratio, xenotypes, ideoligions, wealth, education and employment - derived from the factions pressing on it, their tech and beliefs, and the land itself. Nothing is stored in your save. A single Societies switch turns the whole population layer off for a geography-only game. - Demographic Map Overlays: seven world-map overlays, one per axis, plus faction territory and population density, running on Realistic Planets 2's bundled map-mode framework. - Region Panel Breakdown: the expanded region readout shows the full demographic profile alongside ownership and economics. - Hooks for Other Mods: a public API lets war and drafting mods skew a region's sex ratio (drafts, combat losses) with generational recovery, lets expansion mods rank territory the way core does, and lets companion patches seed their own outposts and holdings at world generation.
*** BEST ON A NEW COLONY - EXISTING SAVES ARE SUPPORTED IN COMPATIBILITY MODE *** A world generated with the mod installed gets everything, including placement rules. A world already in progress is adopted in Compatibility Mode: provinces are drawn and territory is owned and shown, but placement stays with vanilla or whichever mod owns it. The mode is decided once per save and shown under Strict territorial ownership in the mod settings. Removing the mod from an in-progress save is not supported and will log errors.
Requires: Realistic Planets 2, Harmony
--- Changelog (v0.4.0) - Map & Placement --- The world map is redrawn to follow the land, and factions settle it with character. A new-game Geographic Placement dialog puts territory shares, clustering and kin in your hands.
The map follows the land: - Inland lakes are shared between their shores instead of ringing themselves with an unowned border; enclosed water up to a size cap is split along a clean midline that meets at the lake's centre. - Small islands under ten tiles join the nearest landmass; chains of small islands that add up to a real landmass (30+ tiles) become a single archipelago region. - One-to-six-tile slivers are folded into a neighbouring region or dropped when isolated; an Enable small regions setting keeps them as real, settle-able regions if you prefer. - Mountain passes and one-tile land bridges are read as borders, so a region no longer flows through a narrow saddle and spans two places. - Regions are rounder and more natural (a relaxed-honeycomb default); the 0.3.0 balanced-cells look and the 0.2.x boxes are still selectable from the World partition algorithm dropdown. - One Target region size knob replaces the old min/max sliders; sparse biomes scale up automatically, and a Biome region sizes editor lets you retune any biome.
Factions settle with character: - Placement weighs a biome's real liveability - movement, disease, settlement weighting - and avoids crowding, so raiders stop homesteading on the ice and boreal and temperate land fill in as expected. - Per-faction territory clustering: some nations sprawl into one contiguous hold, others keep a set number of separate footholds, and pirates scatter; new footholds are kept spaced apart. - A scattered low-tech faction splits into related kin factions, one per region group, compass-named off the parent and friendly to each other (toggle it off to keep single large factions). - A faction that holds at least half a region counts its natural barriers - coasts, rock and mountain ridges - as a secure border.
The Geographic Placement dialog: - Set the world up before you generate it: a relative-size share per faction with a live "region count" estimate, a share pie (by faction or by hostility), and a hostility dot per faction. A Basic view fits every faction on one screen; an Advanced view exposes resource weights, placement order, clustering and kin. - The region estimate is computed from the real partition model and a calibrated coverage curve, so what you see before generating matches the world you get.
World setup and control: - A Societies master toggle disables the entire population, demographics and economy layer for a geography-only game. - World generation can seed outposts and holdings, with a World maturity slider from an empty frontier to a fully-built world; companion patches can register their own holding types. A region lock governs settling inside a rival's territory and can be toggled mid-game. - Worlds are stamped Worldgen: v0.4.0 and record the settings they were generated with, so regenerating a seed reproduces the same map; existing saves keep their original stamp and are never re-cut.
Performance: - World generation's partition step is about 28 times faster: the mountain-pass split now tests only genuine pinch points instead of every tile, dropping a measured world from ~82 seconds to under 3 with an identical map.
Under the hood: - Removed the unused Population caps checkbox (its multipliers stay). On new worlds, strict territorial ownership, placement governance and settlement tiers now start off for compatibility.
